newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Rugby union-Three Venditti tries sink Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Three Venditti tries sink Ireland.

text.p: A hat-trick of tries from left-wing David Venditti took France to a comfortable 32-15 win over Ireland in their opening Five Nations championship game at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.
Venditti's second try in the 61st minute, converted by Thomas Castaignede, saw France take a 19-15 lead after which the visitors never looked back.
Castaignede landed two late penalties before Venditti scored his third touchdown just before the final whistle to maintain France's good record against the Irish.
The French last lost to Ireland at Lansdowne Road in 1983.
Ireland were in contention for a full hour and in fact dominated the play for a period after fly-half Eric Elwood had put them 15-12 ahead with a penalty in the 50th minute.
Elwood, who last played for Ireland against Scotland a year ago, had kept Ireland in the game in the first half when he landed four penalties from five kicks at goal.
The French, who led 12-6 after 32 minutes, had first half tries from scrum-half Fabien Galthie, which Castaignede converted, and Venditti.

France had both second-row forward Olivier Merle and number eight Fabien Pelous shown yellow cards just before the interval as the Irish, with their supporters roaring them on, pressured their opponents line.
